text:
Leah C: Quick heads-up  I'm updating the provisioning docs to clarify tenant label validation and CLI fallback behavior. customers were confused when invalid labels caused a 400 from the API but the CLI printed a vague 'patch failed' message. need a tiny example + suggested UX wording.

Hector M: saw a support thread on that. short examples + a recommended validation table would help.

Rina P: runtime/cli note: rwctl does client-side basic validation for label format (alphanum + dash), but it doesn't know policy-level label whitelists, so server can still reject. we should show both sides and a suggested cli --force-confirm flag behavior.

Leah C: drafting snippets: suggested YAML example for provisioning snippet users copy: 
```yaml
pool:
  id: example-pool
  placement:
    tenant_isolation:
      labels: ["regulatory-tier-a", "us-west"]
```

Leah C: CLI examples: 
- Safe patch (client-side validation):
`rwctl pool patch --id $POOL --set placement.tenant_isolation.labels=[regulatory-tier-a,us-west]`
- Force-patch (server may still reject if labels disallowed):
`rwctl pool patch --id $POOL --set placement.tenant_isolation.labels=[bad#label] --force`

Hector M: nice. can we add a short table (valid format vs server rejection cause) like: valid format: alphanum/dash; server reject: not in customer whitelist, reserved label, or policy conflict. one-liner each.

Rina P: also add a short SDK snippet (TypeScript) that demonstrates catching the API error and surfacing guidance: 
```ts
try {
  await client.patchPool(poolId, { placement: { tenant_isolation: { labels: ['bad#label'] } } })
} catch (e) {
  if (e.code === 'INVALID_LABEL') console.error('Label format invalid: only alphanumeric and dashes allowed')
  else if (e.code === 'LABEL_DISALLOWED') console.error('Server rejected label: check tenant label whitelist or contact support')
  else throw e
}
```

Leah C: wording suggestion for UX note: "CLI validates label syntax locally; server enforces account- and policy-level restrictions. If a server-side rejection occurs, rwctl will return the server error unless --force is used to bypass client checks (use with caution)." short and explicit.

DevEx-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5601 branch: docs/provisioning/label-validation-ux 

Hector M: one more ask: add a tiny troubleshooting flow in the doc: 1) check CLI error message, 2) run `rwctl inspect pool $POOL` to show allowed labels, 3) contact support if label is expected but rejected. keep it 3 lines.

Rina P: runtime confirms `rwctl inspect` exposes tenant label whitelist when available. add that command to the flow.

Leah C: adding the 3-line flow and a cross-ref to the provisioning index. also fixing a stale relative link CI flagged earlier.

DevEx-bot: CI status: lint ok, link-checker found relative link to docs/dedicated/placement.md (404). Suggested target: /docs/dedicated/placement/labels.md 

Leah C: fixed the link in the branch and pushed.

eng-platform-bot: runtime-approved phrasing: "Client-side validation helps early feedback; server-side rejections indicate policy-level constraints. Use --force only with owner approval." Left INT-2164 ref.

DevEx-bot: PR merged (5601) by Leah C  changes deployed to staging: https://staging.redwood.ai/docs/dedicated/label-validation-ux.html

Hector M: verified staging. small nit: consider adding an example of a reserved label (eg: 'system-core') so customers see a concrete server rejection cause.

Leah C: good idea. adding reserved-label example and merging a tiny follow-up later. closing thread.
